title: A startup that slashes AI agent bills just raised $35M. Anthropic is a backer.
excerpt: Sapiom raised a $35M Series A to cut AI agent running costs, sometimes tenfold. One backer is Anthropic, whose bills the startup is built to shrink.
content_html:
Sapiom is a San Francisco startup that sits between AI agents and the models they run on. It has raised a $35 million Series A. Dragonfly led the round. It comes 11 months after the company launched, and six months after a $15 million seed led by Accel. That takes total funding to $50 million.

The pitch is narrow and timely: make AI agents cheaper to run. At the moment an agent acts, Sapiom decides which model, tool, or service it may use. It enforces a budget before the money is spent. Its Router sends each call to the cheapest capable model, not the most expensive one. The platform has processed more than 270 million transactions since launching six months ago.

The bill that made the case

The clearest case is a customer named Polsia. The AI startup employs nobody, running swarms of agents to help operate other businesses. Its projected revenue jumped from $100,000 to $10 million in a year, Semafor reported. But its token bill climbed with it, hitting $1.2 million a month on Anthropic. After Sapiom ran a series of evaluations, that bill fell roughly tenfold, to about $100,000.

“It’s just unsustainable,” founder Ilan Zerbib told Semafor. He argues that startups cannot deploy at the prices frontier labs charge, even when the demand is there.

Here is the awkward part. Anthropic is one of Sapiom’s investors, returning for the Series A alongside Okta Ventures, Menlo Ventures, and Array Ventures. A model maker is helping fund the startup whose product is spending less on model makers. Zerbib frames it as aligned, not adversarial.

Cheaper inference lets companies build more agents. Some of that work, he argues, will still need the most powerful models.

Cost is the new constraint

Sapiom is riding a shift in how companies talk about AI. Gartner forecasts that companies will cancel more than 40% of agentic AI projects by the end of 2027. Escalating costs are among the leading reasons. Corporate AI budgets are getting their first hard audit. Some firms are already capping what staff can spend. Semafor pointed to a KPMG survey of 2,100 executives in June, in which just 7% could name established returns.

Zerbib’s bet is that the number of agents is about to explode. There may be tens of millions of software developers, he told Semafor. In his words, “we’re talking about trillions of agents that will operate in the economy in the next three years.”

Most of that work, on his numbers, does not need a frontier model. “In 95% of cases, it doesn’t make sense to go to a very expensive frontier model,” he said. TNW has covered how US firms are already swapping frontier models for cheaper ones to control spend.

Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi is joining the board. He calls the gap an infrastructure problem, not a dashboard one. “Agents are becoming employees with no manager and no budget,” he said, “and increasingly, the CTO is the one acting as CFO, allocating real money with no visibility into where it goes.”

A crowded toll booth

Sapiom’s Router puts it up against OpenRouter, the best-known name in model routing. Its difference, per Semafor, is the infrastructure. Sapiom serves open-weight models from its own racks in a San Jose data centre. Most rivals act purely as middlemen. It charges for the compute directly, instead of adding a markup. It is one of a wave of startups selling agent infrastructure to investors this year.

That edge may not last. Routing is starting to look like a commodity. Amazon and Microsoft now bundle it into Bedrock and Azure. Open-source routers are free. OpenRouter alone moves around 25 trillion tokens a week.

One market tracker counts 80 active routing competitors. Sapiom is betting on what it owns underneath: the inference, and the controls around it. That, it hopes, is what separates a feature from a company.

content_html_zh:
Sapiom 是一家位于旧金山的初创公司，位于人工智能代理和它们运行的​​模型之间。 它已筹集了 3500 万美元的 A 轮融资。 蜻蜓队领先本轮。 该公司成立 11 个月后，以及由 Accel 领投的 1500 万美元种子资金六个月后。 这需要总资金达到 5000 万美元。

范围狭窄且及时：让人工智能代理的运行成本更低。 当代理采取行动时，Sapiom 决定它可以使用哪种模型、工具或服务。 它在花钱之前强制执行预算。 它的路由器将每个呼叫发送到最便宜的型号，而不是最昂贵的型号。 自六个月前推出以来，该平台已处理超过 2.7 亿笔交易。

案子的法案

最明显的例子是一位名叫 Polsia 的客户。 这家人工智能初创公司没有雇用任何人，而是运行大量代理来帮助运营其他业务。 据 Semafor 报道，其预计一年收入从 10 万美元跃升至 1,000 万美元。 但其代币费用也随之攀升，在 Anthropic 上每月达到 120 万美元。 Sapiom 进行了一系列评估后，该费用大约下降了十倍，降至约 10 万美元。

“这是不可持续的，”创始人 Ilan Zerbib 告诉 Semafor。 他认为，即使有需求，初创公司也无法按照前沿实验室收取的价格进行部署。

这是尴尬的部分。 Anthropic 是 Sapiom 的投资者之一，与 Okta Ventures、Menlo Ventures 和 Array Ventures 一起回归 A 轮融资。 一家模型制造商正在为一家初创公司提供资金，该初创公司的产品在模型制造商身上的支出较少。 泽比布认为它是一致的，而不是敌对的。

更便宜的推理让公司可以构建更多代理。 他认为，其中一些工作仍然需要最强大的模型。

成本成为新的制约因素

Sapiom 正在改变企业谈论人工智能的方式。 Gartner 预测，到 2027 年底，企业将取消超过 40% 的代理 AI 项目。 成本不断上升是主要原因之一。 企业人工智能预算正在接受首次严格审核。 一些公司已经限制了员工的支出。 Semafor 指出，毕马威 (KPMG) 6 月份对 2,100 名高管进行的一项调查显示，只有 7% 的人能够说出既定回报率。

泽比布的赌注是特工数量即将爆炸。 他告诉 Semafor，可能有数千万软件开发人员。 用他的话来说，“我们正在谈论未来三年将在经济中运作的数万亿个代理人。”

从他的数据来看，大部分工作并不需要前沿模型。 “在 95% 的情况下，采用非常昂贵的前沿模型是没有意义的，”他说。 TNW 报道了美国公司如何将前沿模式更换为更便宜的模式来控制支出。

Dragonfly 的 Haseeb Qureshi 即将加入董事会。 他称这一差距是基础设施问题，而不是仪表板问题。 “代理商正在成为没有经理、没有预算的员工，”他说，“而且首席技术官越来越多地充当首席财务官，分配真实的资金，但无法了解资金的去向。”

拥挤的收费站

Sapiom 的 Router 将其与 OpenRouter 进行对抗，OpenRouter 是模型路由中最知名的名字。 根据 Semafor 的说法，它的区别在于基础设施。 Sapiom 在圣何塞数据中心的自己的机架上提供开放重量模型。 大多数竞争对手纯粹充当中间人。 它直接对计算收费，而不是添加标记。 这是今年向投资者出售代理基础设施的初创公司浪潮之一。

这种优势可能不会持久。 路由开始看起来像一种商品。 亚马逊和微软现在将其捆绑到 Bedrock 和 Azure 中。 开源路由器是免费的。 仅 OpenRouter 每周就转移约 25 万亿个代币。

一位市场跟踪机构统计有 80 家活跃的路由竞争对手。 Sapiom 押注于它所拥有的底层：推理以及围绕它的控制。 它希望这就是功能与公司的区别。
